question: When installing a two-wire (no-neutral) smart light switch, low-wattage LED fixtures often glow or flicker faintly while turned off. What is the primary technical cause of this effect?
options: The switch leaks a small continuous standby current through the load to power itself
High-frequency wireless signals distort the AC sine wave entering the LED driver
The switch automatically defaults to reverse phase-cut mode without a neutral path
Inadequate earthing causes static voltage accumulation inside the fixture housing
explanation: Without a neutral wire, the smart switch completes its internal power circuit by drawing a tiny standby current through the connected light fixture. High-efficiency LEDs can illuminate or flicker on this residual current. Installing a bypass capacitor across the light load resolves the issue.
practical_challenge: How would you determine whether a low-wattage LED circuit requires a bypass capacitor prior to completing a smart switch installation?
